description.value: A legendary stop on the Alaska Highway, Liard River Hot Springs gives touring cyclists access to Canada's second-largest hot spring — a geothermal pool in lush boreal forest — though the 53-site campground fills before noon most summer days.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Primary evidence is the BC Parks website for Liard River Hot Springs Park, which confirms the campground is open year-round, has a 53-site capacity (per OSM), a staffed gatehouse/visitor centre, composting toilet, change house, and boardwalk. The website header shows 'Book camping' prominently, confirming reservations are accepted. OSM records internet_access=no, and neither source mentions showers, laundry, potable water, food nearby, or bike-specific amenities.
concerns: No civic address present in OSM record.

OSM operator contact email (kootenayforestservices@gmail.com) is for the private operator Kootenay Forest Services Ltd., while the listed website is the official BC Parks page — the two contact channels serve different purposes and may confuse users.
Phone number (+1-250-776-7000) listed in OSM was not explicitly confirmed in the fetched website content.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, well-known BC Parks campground on the Alaska Highway that is a classic and highly popular stop for long-distance touring cyclists heading north; the hot springs are a notable draw.
enrichment_extras.notes: The campground is open year-round per the BC Parks website. Facilities at the hot springs include a change house and composting toilet; these serve the day-use hot spring area rather than the campground itself. No internet access per OSM tag.

wow_evidence: Canada's second-largest hot spring — a geothermal pool in lush boreal forest
